articles.title: Israel’s Saied Abu Farchi sent off for gun gesture celebration in defeat by Austria
articles.summary: Forward uses corner flag to simulate gun after equaliser. Nations League match ends in 3-1 loss for Israel. Israel’s forward Saied Abu Farchi was ⁠sent off for celebrating his goal against Austria in ⁠his side’s 3-1 ​Nations League defeat on Thursday by using the corner ⁠flag to simulate a gun.
body: Abu Farchi headed home in the 55th ⁠minute to bring Israel level after ​Austria had ‌taken the lead ‌through a Romano Schmid penalty before ‌half-time at the Raiffeisen Arena in Linz.
The 20-year-old ran to the corner flag, grabbed it and made a gun-firing gesture during his celebration.
The ‌referee had booked Abu Farchi four minutes earlier and showed ​him a second yellow card for the celebration, leaving Israel with 10 players.
Austria regained ⁠the lead in the 90th minute through ​Phillipp ​Mwene, who scored via Paul ​Wanner’s cross. ‌Sasa Kalajdzic ​added ​a third in stoppage time with a close-range finish.

articles.title: ‘It’s not in us’: Anthony Gordon backs Tuchel over England’s possession problem
articles.summary: Barcelona winger says England cannot play like Spain. Gordon: ‘The Mexico game set us up a bit’ Anthony Gordon has sided with Thomas Tuchel’s assertion that controlling games through possession is not part of English football’s DNA.
body: England’s perennial struggle to keep the ball when under pressure flared when a place in the final was within touching distance in July, allowing Argentina to fight back and go through with two late goals. The pain has not gone away and there has been intense scrutiny of Tuchel’s role in Atlanta. The head coach’s tactical choices were criticised and he faced a backlash after saying “ball possession” was not in his team’s DNA.

But Gordon, who thinks he will always be scarred by losing against Argentina, sided with Tuchel’s observations about England’s style as he looked towards the Nations League game against Spain on Saturday. The 25-year-old admitted the side had an ingrained inability to control games but argued they should stop trying to copy other nations.
Gordon has gained an insight into the Spanish understanding of how to use the ball since his move to Barcelona. His view is that England should lean more into their physical strengths.

articles.title: 'Don't put pressure on us' over Israel games - Republic of Ireland's Ogbene
articles.summary: Republic of Ireland winger Chiedozie Ogbene urges the public to not "put the pressure on us" over the campaign to boycott the upcoming Nations League games against Israel.
body: The sides are due to meet in Debrecen, Hungary on Sunday before the return fixture in Backa Topola, Serbia on 4 October (both 19:45 BST).

Since the sides were drawn together in Group B3, there has been increasing calls in Ireland to withdraw from the games due to the ongoing situation in Gaza with a 'Stop The Game' campaign gathering pace.

In the lead up to Thursday's 1-0 defeat by Kosovo in Pristina stand-in captain Dara O'Shea confirmed the players would meet on Friday to discuss their approach to Sunday's 'home' game for Israel, which will have no Irish fans in attendance before their behind-closed-doors match the following week.
"I'm aware of the feelings towards it," Ogbene told RTE Sport after Thursday's loss.

articles.title: Gakpo denies Klopp perfect start as Xavi’s Netherlands rescue draw against Germany
articles.summary: Jürgen Klopp had predicted his bow as Germany manager could be wild, a trait he would accept as long as his team looked lively. He got both in a strange, frayed and at times alarmingly pinball-like game that ended with a dramatic Netherlands equaliser and mounting injury worries.
body: At least Germany can be sure it will not be dull. Jürgen Klopp had predicted his debut as head coach could be wild, a trait he would accept as long as his team were lively enough. Both transpired in a frayed, pinball-like game whose lack of quality could be forgiven on account of its entertainment levels. The Netherlands more than merited a brilliant late equaliser from Cody Gakpo and by the time those present had drawn breath it felt appropriate that, for all the talk of new dawns, everyone finished back where they had started.

World domination is a far-off prospect for both of these flailing giants on such scrappy, frenetic evidence. But at least those with a stake in this famous old fixture, largely shorn of the spite and spit that defined it of old, could come away feeling something. Restoring those essential sensations of joy, pain and meaning sits at the very top of Klopp’s priorities. Germany looked raw and scattergun for long periods, reined in only by their lack of technical aptitude, but there were signs of an energy that had long been missing.

articles.title: João Félix strike for Portugal enough to sink Wales but Ronaldo fever falls flat
articles.summary: There was a comic-strip feel to another eventful evening in the world of Cristiano Ronaldo. Where to start? It was the 67th minute when his No 7 went up on the fourth official’s board, prompting Ronaldo to remove the captain’s armband from his left bicep before departing to a universal ovation, but…
body: The referee, Donatas Rumsas, hurried him off the pitch but Ronaldo, his hair glazed copper, was presumably ruminating on a series of missed chances, a sitter from a few yards at the start of the second half, and his disallowed goal, after skating offside to latch on to a Bruno Fernandes pass. The grandiose “Siu” celebration went to waste, though try telling that to the locals who worship him.

In the end, Portugal began their defence of the Nations League with a narrow victory courtesy of another Al-Nassr forward, João Felix’s deflected first-half strike from the edge of the box beating Danny Ward in goal.

Many of the Wales squad have been lightly raced of late, but they could have snatched a late equaliser when Brennan Johnson hit the crossbar and Rúben Dias desperately denied Lewis Koumas, who again impressed Craig Bellamy. For Wales, this was an exhaustive physical effort and afterwards the Wales head coach, citing his own experiences as a player, referenced how mentally sapping games against elite opposition can prove. “I needed an ice pack on my head,” Bellamy said.

articles.title: Buttler injury halts England as Sri Lanka level series
articles.summary: Jos Buttler's bravery comes in vain as Sri Lanka fight back to beat England in the second one-day international at Headingley and set up a series decider at The Oval.
body: Needing 68 from 75 balls, England were cruising towards a target of 322 until Buttler retired hurt on 67 after tweaking a hamstring.
When Rehan Ahmed, Gus Atkinson and Jamie Overton fell, Buttler re-emerged with 27 needed from 14 balls and witnessed Will Jacks fall for 52 at the non-striker's end.
England were left needing 19 from the last with Buttler on strike but, barely able to hobble a single, he holed out at deep mid-wicket. England finished on 306-9 as Sri Lanka won by 16 runs.

Buttler had earlier shown flashes of his vintage best in hitting Sri Lanka's spinners for five sixes, putting England on course after collapse of 3-14 spoiled an opening stand of 143 between Tom Banton and Ben Duckett.

articles.title: New York Yankees vs. Tampa Bay Rays: Cam Schlittler vs. Ian Seymour
articles.summary: Team results over individual accolades is not even a discussion to be had most of the time, but specifically in a game like this, I’d be remiss not to state the importance of the latter.
body: Schlittler's work to fill in as the one ace from start to finish of this impressive pitching staff has named him the odds-on favorite to win the AL Cy Young Award. And why stop there? Some (like Josh) might even argue he should be in the MVP consideration, helping this team navigate a mostly Aaron Judge-less season. How much stock to put into it almost doesn't matter; just the fact that there is a reasonable argument to be made shows just how impressive this young starter has been.

When Schlittler dominated the Red Sox in a historic playoff performance last season to take the Yankees to the ALDS, most of us probably felt he couldn't surprise us further in the near future. Yet, here we are with a season beyond everyone's wildest dreams.

With a left-handed starter on the mound for the Rays in Ian Seymour, the Yankees lean on the platoon advantages apart from the catching position, as Austin Wells is back behind the plate to catch Schlittler. Amed Rosario gets the nod at the hot corner despite Ryan McMahon 's grand slam last night, and José Caballero receives a rare start in center. Fingers crossed that this defensive lineup gets the job done for the Yankees' ace.

articles.title: Alcaraz felt burnt out after too much exposure on and off the court
articles.summary: Carlos Alcaraz has admitted feeling burnt out due to being exposed to a lot of commitments before he suffered a lengthy layoff due to an injury sustained in April.
body: The Spaniard, who won the Australian Open title at the start of the year, was forced to miss more than four months from tennis because of a right wrist injury.
Alcaraz returned at the US Open where he reached the quarter-finals before losing a five-set thriller to American Ben Shelton, which finished at 3.33am local time.
Due to the demanding nature of the calendar, the former world No 1 has said he plans to take longer breaks from the game in the future and skip some tournaments.
"With the breaks I cannot plan them in advance," Alcaraz told Sky's Jacquie Beltrao at London's O2. "It depends how I feel mentally and physically.

articles.title: NBA Hall of Famer and former Hawks star Bob Pettit dead at 93
articles.summary: NEW ORLEANS - Bob Pettit, the former St. Louis Hawks star who won the NBA’s first MVP award and later had his No. 9 retired by the Atlanta Hawks, has died at 93. [DOWNLOAD: Free WSB-TV News app for alerts as news breaks ] Pettit’s alma mater, LSU, announced Thursday that he died a day earlier.
body: Pettit played 11 NBA seasons, all with the Hawks and made the All-Star team in every season.
He led the Hawks to the 1958 NBA title against the Boston Celtics, the franchise’s only championship.
Pettit also won the NBA MVP award in 1959 and earned All-Star game MVP honors four times.
He retired after the 1964-65 season with career averages of 26.4 points and 16.2 rebounds.

articles.title: Late Gakpo strike denies Klopp winning start with Germany
articles.summary: Cody Gakpo hit a stoppage-time volley to earn the Netherlands a 1-1 draw against Germany in their Nations League Group A2 opener on Thursday, denying Jurgen Klopp victory in his first match as Germany boss.
body: Former Liverpool manager Klopp took charge in July after their surprise early exit from the World Cup against Paraguay in the last 32 under Julian Nagelsmann.
His side appeared set to give him the perfect start after Felix Nmecha put Germany ahead, but Gakpo finished off a swift counter-attack in the closing stages to level the contest.

The result also gave Xavi Hernandez something to celebrate in his first game in charge of the Netherlands. He was appointed in August after Ronald Koeman stepped down following the Dutch side's elimination at the same stage of the World Cup.

Germany suffered an early blow when Jamal Musiala was ruled out before kick-off, after experiencing muscle pain - and they were given a scare when Virgil van Dijk headed in from a corner inside the first 15 minutes.

articles.title: Scheffler edges final-hole thriller as Team USA grab Presidents Cup lead
articles.summary: Team USA made a solid start to their bid for an 11th consecutive Presidents Cup victory by building a 3-2 lead in Thursday's fourballs session against the International Team.
body: Brandt Snedeker's side have historically dominated the biennial contest but were presented with a tough test on the opening day at Medinah Country Club, where the Internationals won two of the five points on offer.

World No 1 Scottie Scheffler ended his winless record alongside Sam Burns by edging a final-hole thriller against Min Woo Lee and Sungjae Im, following Justin Thomas partnering rookie Jackson Koivun to a 4&3 win over Corey Conners and Nico Echavarria.

The all-Japanese pairing of Hideki Matsuyama and Ryo Hisatsune despatched Cameron Young and Xander Schauffele 3&1, before Wyndham Clark and Collin Morikawa beat Ryan Fox and Adam Scott 3&2 to ensure Team USA would win the session.

The United States have led after the opening day in nine of the last 10 Presidents Cups, although Tom Kim and Si Woo Kim reduced their advantage by seeing off Chris Gotterup and Patrick Cantlay 3&2 in the bottom match.
